CANONICAL_NAME.value: Redlock (antirez, 2014) as redlock-py, with Debian's redis-server as the lock store -- a lease-based distributed mutex, and the design Kleppmann's 2016 analysis argued is unsafe for correctness-critical use

VERSION.value: github.com/SPSCommerce/redlock-py master as of 2026-09-13 (commit in hashes); redis-server 7.0 (Debian bookworm) at run time

value.lineage: A LEASE-based distributed mutex: acquire a key with a TTL on a majority of N independent Redis instances within a validity window; release by a check-and-delete script. Proposed by Antirez (redis.io/topics/distlock, 2014); criticised by Martin Kleppmann ('How to do distributed locking', 2016) for depending on bounded clock drift and process pauses, with Antirez's reply ('Is Redlock safe?'). Preserved as a runnable lease mechanism AND as a documented contested design (Phase 9: incorrect timing assumption).

value.built_to: grant one client at a time exclusive access to a resource across machines, with a lease so a crashed holder cannot block forever
value.pressure: crashes of holders, network delay, clock drift, process pauses (GC) -- the last two are exactly the contested assumptions
value.success_means: mutual exclusion while the lease is valid; liveness after a holder dies

value.pressure: partial failure, unbounded delay, unsynchronised clocks
value.failure_condition: two holders at once after a pause or clock jump (Kleppmann's scenario); or permanent blocking without a lease

cut.note: a lease-based distributed mutex over N independent Redis instances: acquire the same key with a unique random value and a TTL on each instance; the lock is held only if a majority acknowledged within a validity window that subtracts the elapsed acquisition time and a clock-drift margin from the TTL; release is a check-and-delete Lua script that deletes the key only if its value still matches the acquirer's, so a lease that already expired and was retaken is never deleted by the old holder

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: Redlock.lock (72-120): val = 22 random chars; drift = ttl * 0.01 + 2; per server SET resource val NX PX ttl; validity = ttl - elapsed - drift; hold if validity > 0 and n >= quorum, else unlock everywhere and retry; quorum = N // 2 + 1
organs.mechanism: a unique value identifies this acquisition; the client sets the key with NX (only if absent) and PX (a millisecond TTL) on each of the N servers, timing the whole round; the lock is granted only if at least a majority set succeeded AND the remaining validity (TTL minus the time the round took minus a drift allowance) is still positive; if either fails the client deletes its value from every server and retries after a delay; the drift margin (1 percent of the TTL plus 2 ms) accounts for clock differences between the client and the servers
organs.input: a resource name and a TTL
organs.output: a Lock (validity, resource, value) or False
organs.state: none on the client beyond the returned lock
assumptions: a majority of independent, non-colluding Redis instances is available; clocks drift by less than the margin over the lease; the network round trip is much shorter than the TTL (else validity goes negative)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: mutual exclusion without a single point of failure, from plain Redis instances
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the algorithm was criticised (Kleppmann 2016) because a process pause or clock jump longer than the validity window lets two holders believe they hold the lock; the validity return value is the client's own honest bound, not a guarantee the resource enforces

organs.human_name: Redlock.unlock (121-132) and unlock_script: 'if redis.call(get, KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then return redis.call(del, KEYS[1]) else return 0'; unlock_instance runs it on every server
organs.mechanism: release runs one Lua script per server that atomically compares the stored value with the acquirer's unique value and deletes the key only on a match; because the compare and delete are one server-side script they cannot interleave, and because the value is unique per acquisition, a holder whose lease already expired (and whose key was retaken by another client with a different value) cannot delete the new holder's lock
organs.output: the key removed where it still belongs to the caller
assumptions: the get-and-delete must be atomic (hence a script, not two calls); the value must be unpredictable and unique so no other client can forge a release
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: safe release even after a lease lapses; the mistake it prevents (a plain DEL that could delete someone else's lock) is the reason for the script
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: if the server is unreachable at release the key lingers until its TTL, which is acceptable; MultipleRedlockException surfaces per-server errors

rejected_cuts.candidate: the CLI (cli.py), setup.py, the connection-parsing in __init__ (url / dict / object forms), the retry-count and delay bookkeeping

rejected_cuts.evidence: the majority-acquire-with-validity and the check-and-delete release are separable; the atlas's cocagne-plain-paxos and willemt-raft hold the consensus alternatives to a lease

pressures.source_evidence: Redlock.lock; the unlock script; the distlock note and Kleppmann's critique (record)
pressures.condition: N independent stores with expiring keys; many clients race for one resource; stores and clients crash; clocks are imperfect; the score is whether two clients ever both believe they hold the lock, and whether the resource is ever left locked forever
pressures.resource_or_constraint: N stores; a TTL; a drift margin
pressures.failure_condition: two simultaneous holders (a safety violation), or a permanently locked resource after a crash
pressures.world_punishes: a single store (a point of failure); a plain DEL release; ignoring elapsed time and drift
pressures.world_rewards: majority acquisition, a validity window, unique-value check-and-delete, TTL expiry
pressures.observable_consequence: the count of double-holds and stuck locks under injected store crashes, client pauses and clock skew, for the majority+validity algorithm vs a single-store lock; the sensitivity of double-holds to a pause longer than the validity
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a linearizable consensus service (Raft/Paxos, in this atlas) which the world may offer as the stronger control
pressures.cheat_control: a Raft-backed lock must show zero double-holds under the same faults; the single-store lock must fail when that store crashes; Redlock must hold except when a pause exceeds the validity (Kleppmann's case): the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: distributed mutual exclusion over Redis (antirez 2014)
